authoring: Hand-authored from the work order of the priority review (section 6) and updated by the iteration-6 cycles. Validated at build time by repurposing_view.py: every need id must exist in the needs register, the entries follow the order of the needs register (no ranking), the kind must agree with the F/C/P positions the view assigns to that need, and the dates are ISO dates. The research-update date is shown apart from the catalogue build date. No score, no probability, no ranking of treatments or of needs. Window states (P7, rescue-window record section 5) are a closed vocabulary; for cards the build checks that the card wording itself carries the early-window statement.

entries.question: Does an intermediate vector level separate a threshold from a gradient, and is the benefit only prevented inside the first days of life or also recovered when treatment follows onset? No study has measured the phenotype at the day of injection.
entries.data: The cards' own next measurement: an intermediate arm defined as a fraction of the higher level, carried to 300 days with survival, weight, glucose, ECoG and quantified myelination; plus a pre-treatment baseline in the same animals or an age-matched cohort, and treated-after-onset arms with a same-age untreated comparator (organoids or a slower-onset model). Added in IT8: a post-onset arm in organoids with a same-organoid baseline and an AAV9 vector control, severe and milder variant classes side by side. External precedents (batch ORCH-SCIBATCH-DR-20261105): the added arm should be worded per endpoint class and should measure the restoration actually achieved at the age of treatment and its regional distribution, because the one comparable later-age failure in a short-lived null was left uninterpretable by that missing measurement; carry a within-animal pre-treatment recording, a treated wild-type or heterozygote arm, growth and glycaemia as primary endpoints (growth failed even with pre-onset treatment in the closest analogue), and follow-up long enough to see decay. Quantified myelin sheath structure (g-ratio or electron microscopy, not marker intensity) is the discriminating endpoint for a neuron-driven lesion: white-matter abnormality has been reversed after a documented onset only in glial or metabolic lesions, and sheath structure after onset has been reported only in a metabolic oligodendrocyte-enzyme lesion (G-ratio by electron microscopy, one source) and not in any neuron-driven lesion. Spike-wave rate is the confirmatory endpoint and its external precedent is split, so pair it with a rhythm or power-spectrum measure; interneuron number as well as excitability, because no source measured number.
entries.would_change: Quantified myelination would add a controlled row on the same need; a failure would move the card to C2 by rule; a treated-after-onset arm would show whether the word recovery may be used for that endpoint. A post-onset arm that moved a circuit readout but not quantified sheath structure would match the precedents. The reverse pattern would be the first of its kind for a neuron-driven lesion measured as sheath structure, not the first outright. Either would need the locator audit before it touched a card.
entries.feasibility: Wet-lab work in a Wwox-null mouse by a laboratory that has the vector; none known in this repository; the source laboratory is one group (the two papers share a senior author). Whether the vector is obtainable: not known. External precedents sharpen rather than relieve the problem: no external post-onset arm treats an animal with the lifespan of this null; two external sources treated nulls with short lives later with a modest survival benefit (abstract level), so a vector contribution to the perinatal-only window is possible and unmeasured.

window_state.note: Mouse: every endpoint is read after treatment at P0 to P5 in animals never measured before it.

Only organoid hyperexcitability: AAV9 given at week 10 on a phenotype recorded at week 7 (post-onset by about 3 weeks, in different organoid cohorts), read at week 16 only; persistence not measured; one endpoint family; radial-glia abnormalities not corrected.
Any mouse treatment after P5, a pre-treatment baseline, reversibility.

entries.summary_it: Capire se l'aggiunta del gene giova solo se data nei primi giorni di vita (prevenzione) o anche dopo la comparsa del fenotipo, e se la dose intermedia distingue soglia da gradiente.
entries.feasibility_it: Laboratorio con il vettore e un topo Wwox-nullo; nessuno noto nel repository. Se il vettore sia ottenibile: non nota.

entries.question: Is the Q230P-class protein made and then cleared, by which route (proteasome, lysosome), and does any protein that returns carry function per molecule? The favourable support is outside WWOX only and the abstaining cards wait on the same unmeasured branch.
entries.data: A route-and-function experiment on the exact variant in an isogenic WWOX-null human neural line: soluble, pellet and native fractions, half-life, transgene mRNA, route arms and a viability readout in every arm, read against a wild-type function ruler (cards A01 and A02 next measurement; P5 reference for the ruler; outcomes fixed in advance).
entries.would_change: No protein with synthesis present closes A02 and A05 for this allele; soluble native protein on the ruler would give the first WWOX-system row on the need; protein without function would give C1; a lysosome-only effect would show the proteasome lever is wrong for this lesion class.
entries.feasibility: A cell line expressing the variant is not held; the design is complete, but the function ruler it depends on is a design and not yet validated.
entries.summary_it: Capire se la proteina Q230P viene prodotta e poi eliminata, per quale via, e se quella che torna è funzionante.
entries.feasibility_it: Linea cellulare con la variante non disponibile; disegno completo ma il righello di funzione non è ancora validato.

entries.question: Is the ISR kinase arm active at all in WWOX-deficient neural cells, and is it compensatory or harmful? After the mouse P17 transcripts the sign is unresolved, and two mitochondrial-lesion precedents have opposite signs (protective in one, harmful in the other); neuronal activity alone also raises ATF4 protein without an mRNA change.
entries.data: Protein and phosphorylation readouts (phospho-eIF2alpha against total, ATF4 protein, targets, translation) in isogenic WWOX-null against corrected neural lines at matched maturity, with and without activity silencing, sampled before, at and after the first hyperexcitability, with challenge arms and kinase attribution by genetics; the decision table is fixed before the run.
entries.would_change: A measured elevation would give the need its first controlled WWOX-system row on the pathway; a flat result removes the premise of F3 for card E01. Transcripts alone cannot do either: the mouse analysis found no resolvable sign at about 0.3.
entries.feasibility: No suitable dataset is held (the progenitor deposit failed its pre-declared gates; the mouse deposits hold transcripts only); availability of isogenic lines: not known.
entries.summary_it: Capire se la risposta integrata allo stress è attiva nelle cellule neurali prive di WWOX, se compensa o danneggia e quanto dipende dall'attività di rete: oggi il segno è discordante.
entries.feasibility_it: Nessun insieme di dati adatto in mano; disponibilità di linee isogeniche: non nota.

entries.question: Is PDH phosphorylation higher in WWOX-deficient neural cells, and does a PDK inhibitor change it in a genotype-dependent way without lowering glucose in a hypoglycaemic model?
entries.data: The closing condition of card I01: PDHA1 Ser293 phosphorylation, total PDH, activity and a tracer experiment, genotype by inhibitor; a glycaemia arm in the constitutive knockout, where glucose at P10 is already about 95 against about 130. IT7 P6 2026-10-29: decisive measurement unchanged; read PDK1, LDHA, LDHB, HK2, SLC2A1 and BNIP3 transcripts beside it in the same cells, so the replicated WWOX-deficient human neural contrast that the P3 comparison named as missing is also a second transfer test; no computational ranking selects the compound arm. (IT7 P6: the network routes added no value and the signature route was not detected, not excluded.) IT8 P3 2026-10-29, restated IT9 P4a 2026-10-30: a nanomolar pan-isoform inhibitor is added alongside dichloroacetate for the genotype-by-inhibitor arm, because dichloroacetate inhibits the recombinant human kinase isoforms only at about 0.1 to above 5 millimolar in curated database rows and a null with it alone at cell-attainable concentrations would be uninterpretable, whereas in the one document that measured both on all four isoforms the inhibitor acts at about 20 to 170 nanomolar; caveats: pan-isoform (no isoform attribution), availability for research use not stated by the sources, neuronal engagement and brain exposure not shown, second-isoform assay on a different substrate. IT9 P6 2026-10-30 (card K01): the HIF axis upstream of PDK1 is a separate, conditional experiment that can share cells and lysates with this one: HIF-1alpha and HIF-2alpha protein in WWOX-deficient versus corrected human neural cells first (never measured; nuclear and cytoplasmic fractions, normoxia and hypoxia), then genetic HIF1A and EPAS1 knockdown and a PX-478-class lever, with a genetic-first arm C (VHL or EGLN1 loss; a prolyl-hydroxylase inhibitor only beside HIF-null and prolyl-hydroxylase-null controls, direction conditional (H-protect), not a 'mimic' of a disease direction) in knockout and corrected cells; deciding readout lactate or acidification and glucose uptake plus PGK1, ALDOA, ENO1, PFKP and PKM individually (the six readout genes and the 10-gene set are guard-scope members: a change there confirms the seed, it does not validate a lever), with network activity and viability giving the valence; the arms are conditional on the HIF-dependent shift being adaptive or harmful. IT10 P5 2026-10-31 (restated after IT10 P2.1): step 0 is run at 5 percent oxygen (physioxia) as the primary condition beside 21 and 1 percent, with a hypoxia marker and size matching in any organoid arm, an activity-silenced arm and a MYC loss-of-function arm for the rival explanations, a multielectrode network-activity readout, and two independent knockout clones with isogenic add-back. IT12 2026-10-31: (a) in vivo anchor added to step 0: HIF protein by compartment with hydroxylation, pimonidazole and lactate in perfusion-fixed or in-situ frozen P47T hippocampus and cortex, per-animal seizure count as covariate, a pre-onset age group; (b) the target panel is read gene by gene (Bhlhe40, Ddit4, Ndrg1, Egln3, Ankrd37, Adm beside Pgk1, Aldoa, Pkm, Pfkp); (c) the activity-silenced arm is decisive for the in-vivo question. Reason: the adult P47T transcripts show a broad glycolytic-enzyme shift and not the organoid's selective pattern, so three hypotheses stay apart (organoid state, activity, composition). Reopenable searches from the genetic-interaction screen GSE298081 (one unreplicated clone; association only): a second clone or re-expression screen, a neural genetic-interaction readout including LDHA, PDHA1, SLC2A1, HK2 and HIF1A, a DepMap bulk test, a ChEMBL retry (triggers NP1B1 to NP1B4).
entries.would_change: A genotype-by-inhibitor interaction would give the first WWOX-system row for DCA on this need; the known glucose-lowering and neuropathy signals would remain as tags. A computational ranking of compounds does not change this: the IT7 P3 comparison found no added value for the network routes and an effect not detected, not excluded for the signature route, so the kind of study and the position of the need are unchanged. A null with dichloroacetate alone is not read as absence of a PDK effect. The HIF experiment (card K01) would change a different decision: a negative premise measurement drops the HIF axis for neural cells; knockdown that lowers lactate while viability or differentiation worsen marks the shift as adaptive and drops the lever; the opposite marks it harmful and gives the first WWOX-system row for the lever (F3 to F2 by rule); lactate falling with viability, network activity and differentiation unchanged or discordant leaves the valence unresolved. It does not change the position of the PDK arm of this need. IT12: nothing here moves the position; a protein-level HIF datum in P47T tissue or in human neural cells that separates activity, composition and a WWOX-specific effect would.
entries.feasibility: Human fibroblast precedent exists at abstract level; the WWOX-deficient cells (organoids from a public deposit) need an access request that exists as a draft only and is not to be filed from here.
entries.summary_it: Capire se la fosforilazione di PDH è più alta nelle cellule neurali prive di WWOX e se un inibitore di PDK la modifica in modo dipendente dal genotipo, aggiungendo un inibitore nanomolare pan-isoforma accanto al dicloroacetato (con riserve su selettività e disponibilità). In più (IT9 P6): un esperimento condizionale sull'asse HIF (proteina HIF-1alfa e HIF-2alfa nelle cellule neurali prive di WWOX, poi knockdown genetico e una leva di classe PX-478 contro un controllo di direzione), proposto e non eseguito. Restato (IT10 P2.1/P5): la direzione del cambiamento di HIF non è stabilita (condizionale); controllo genetico per primo; ossigeno fisiologico al 5% come condizione primaria; bracci per attività, MYC e stato di coltura. IT12: nel cervello P47T adulto (solo trascritti) lo spostamento e' ampio e modesto, guidato dagli enzimi glicolitici, e non riproduce il profilo selettivo dell'organoide; restano separate tre ipotesi (stato dell'organoide, attivita', composizione); aggiunti ancoraggio in vivo e pannello genico.
entries.feasibility_it: Precedente in fibroblasti umani a livello di abstract; le cellule WWOX-deficienti richiedono una richiesta di accesso solo in bozza, non inoltrata da qui.

entries.question: Is LDH activity or lactate raised in WWOX-deficient neural cells? (IT8 P3 2026-10-29: the former second half of this question, whether stiripentol reaches an inhibitory level at all, is answered without enzyme-level support on primary data and is no longer asked of it.)
entries.data: Card E02 next measurement: lactate and LDH activity in WWOX-deficient human neural cells, the fly Ldh-alone arm and Wwox mRNA in the double line; the 42 to 500 micromolar LDH range is withdrawn as an exposure target for stiripentol (IT8 P3, below). IT7 P6 2026-10-29: read LDHA and LDHB activity separately (LDHB was the discordant gene in the P47T transfer test); no computational ranking selects the compound arm. (IT7 P6: the network routes added no value and the signature route was not detected, not excluded.) IT8 P3 2026-10-29, restated IT9 P4a 2026-10-30: the compound arm is a nanomolar human-LDHA inhibitor chosen from the curated target entries (205 qualify; 116 have no LDHB datum, 89 have a same-document LDHA and LDHB pair, of which only 2 are 30 fold or more on every pair, so selectivity over LDHB is to be established per compound); stiripentol stays only as a complex I and GABA-A comparator. Datum: enzyme data giving 7 percent inhibition at 2 millimolar and about 10 percent at 0.5 millimolar, no fitted LDH potency among its 88 curated rows (all read; one 2022 cell-level mouse-hepatocyte oxalate-output signal weighed, not decisive), a US label that names no LDH mechanism; stiripentol is not sufficiently supported as an LDH-engagement probe; the 42 to 500 micromolar figure is a secondary range.
entries.would_change: If lactate is not raised, the need loses its WWOX observation and E02 moves to P3 by rule; if raised, the node is tested with a nanomolar human-LDHA inhibitor, not with stiripentol (IT8 P3), and a stiripentol effect would be read as complex I or GABA-A pharmacology. A computational ranking of compounds does not change this: the IT7 P3 comparison found no added value for the network routes and an effect not detected, not excluded for the signature route, so the kind of study and the position of the need are unchanged.
entries.feasibility: Cell lines and fly stocks: not known. A public request draft exists in this directory, but registration or contact is not performed from here.
entries.summary_it: Capire se lattato o attività LDH sono aumentati nelle cellule neurali prive di WWOX; per lo stiripentolo non c'è sostegno a livello enzimatico da dati primari, e il test del nodo usa un inibitore nanomolare di LDHA umana la cui selettività su LDHB è da stabilire.
entries.feasibility_it: Linee cellulari e stock di mosca: non nota; nessuna richiesta o contatto eseguiti da qui.

entries.question: Which of three readings (NMDAR gain, permissive necessity, AMPAR-led drive) explains the d-APV-sensitive bursting, and does the bursting depend on the magnesium block? The d-APV result alone does not separate them.
entries.data: Card F04, step E1: the isolated NMDAR current under voltage control (AMPAR and GABA-A blocked) in knockout, heterozygote and wild-type slices: amplitude, decay, NMDA:AMPA ratio, GluN2B and GluN2A shares, resting potential and input resistance; then concentration-response of d-APV and of a GluN2B-selective tool, and a use-dependent pore blocker (memantine as a translation probe, with Mg2+ and holding potential stated). Card P11: a graded bath-Mg2+ titration in the source medium with d-APV as ceiling, the composition of the recording bath, and serum and cerebrospinal-fluid Mg in the knockout mouse. The graded memantine against perampanel design of card F01 is superseded as discriminator by F04. Added in IT13 (P3b): the only human firing recovery (PMID 42397075 Fig 6) needs a wild-type + WWOX arm and a mutant WWOX arm (WW1-dead and an SDR-region mutant, with construct expression, stability and localisation shown, since a mutant is not necessarily inactive for every WWOX function) to separate recovery from a transgene effect, the organoid as the unit of testing (not ROIs or fields), at least two differentiations, an assessor blind to arm, and two independent silencers (a sodium-channel blocker and an NMDAR antagonist, with a 2-week washout) read on firing and on the CTIP2/SATB2 fraction together: read the effect against the exposure that is still active (a compound can be withdrawn, an AAV transgene keeps being expressed), and report apart an acute effect on an endpoint, a functional benefit during exposure, compensation of an impaired function, a change that persists after a compound is withdrawn, and broader recovery of WWOX functions; a reduction of firing needs controls against toxicity, cell loss and generalised suppression of activity (viability, cell number, preserved evoked responses) before it is read as a functional improvement (see the corrected bench protocol sheet). Added in IT13 (P3a): in the same neuron-deleted slices, resting potential and the M-current (Kv7) component, the isolated NMDAR current and sIPSC, littermate controls and animals as units, matched-trigger wild-type slices, a GluN2B negative allosteric modulator concentration-response beside d-APV and a Kv7 opener with reversal by an M-current blocker (prediction per reading in the design notes): a state that is secondary to illness, myelin or maturation would predict no lever. IT15 refinement: the quantity to measure is the GluN2B-sensitive share of the isolated NMDAR current (a saturating GluN2B negative modulator in the same cells). The expected current fall of a GluN2B modulator is an upper bound (incomplete inhibition, triheteromers), so burst scoring is read against an equal-current titration of a competitive glutamate-site antagonist and a low-trapping pore blocker, with a GluN2A modulator and a second, chemically unrelated GluN2B modulator as controls; a steeper-than-linear burst fall is not a discriminator alone because burst generation is threshold-like. Pore blockers show no subunit selectivity detected in recombinant-receptor data, which are not slice values.
entries.would_change: E1 decides whether an NMDAR gain is present or the dependence is permissive; a partial blocker is read only after E1, and without E1 a memantine result cannot be attributed to pyramidal receptors. A titration that cannot lower bursts inside a reachable range closes the magnesium strand. A silencer that lowers firing without raising CTIP2/SATB2 would be read as separating the two readouts (and as symptomatic only if the controls show generalised suppression); one that raises the markers would be read as an activity-dependent route to the marker readout; lowered firing in wild type + WWOX would limit how much of the add-back effect is attributed to recovery, without cancelling the result in the knockout.
entries.feasibility: Slice electrophysiology in the neuron-specific knockout of the original paper; the line is not held here and whether it is obtainable is not known. Magnesium products have US label evidence by name only; Italy was not checked.
entries.summary_it: Capire quale di tre letture spiega lo scoppio di attività nelle fette (guadagno NMDAR, dipendenza permissiva, spinta AMPAR) e se dipende dal blocco da magnesio; serve prima la corrente NMDAR isolata (E1). IT13: servono bracci WT+WWOX e WWOX mutato (morto), l'organoide come unità, cieco, e due silenziatori indipendenti con lavaggio; la scarica da sola resta sintomatica.
entries.feasibility_it: Elettrofisiologia su fette del knockout neurone-specifico dell'articolo originale: la linea non è disponibile qui, se sia ottenibile non nota; magnesio: etichette USA per nome, Italia non verificata.

entries.question: In the Wwox neuron-deleted neocortical slice, is the lost fast GABA-A inhibition the step that makes bursting (rather than a graded change of resting potential and input resistance, an excitatory gain, or a secondary state)? The heterozygote shares the input-resistance change and is intermediate in resting potential, yet it bursts far less (4 of 23 slices against 36 of 42); the source tests heterozygote against knockout for sIPSC amplitude and frequency (7 heterozygote cells from 4 animals) but reports no heterozygote-versus-wild-type test and no heterozygote mean.
entries.data: Same-cell triad in knockout, heterozygote and Cre-positive wild-type slices: isolated NMDAR current, sIPSC charge with physiological chloride (the source used a KCl internal solution), miniature IPSCs in TTX as the locus readout, and resting potential with input resistance; then, in wild-type and heterozygote slices, a sufficiency matrix (titrate one deficit at a time to its knockout-measured size and ask which gives NMDAR-dependent bursts), then single-mechanism corrections in knockout slices with viability, action-potential height and washout as requirements, the firing-current curve and input resistance measured and reported, and the effect in wild-type slices as a specificity qualifier (not a condition for partial benefit). The animal is the unit; slices from one animal are not independent, and no sample size is fixed here because the variance is not known (see the design notes of the research package).
entries.would_change: A heterozygote with inhibition like the knockout would put the NMDAR/excitatory-gain readings first; a knockout-specific receptor-limited loss would make positive modulation of GABA-A receptors a probe-level compensation hypothesis (subtype selectivity of the candidate agents is disputed across three primary papers); a release-limited loss would favour GABA reuptake inhibition as the contrast; a secondary state would predict no lever. None of these outcomes is a treatment claim.
entries.feasibility: Slice electrophysiology in the neuron-specific knockout of the source laboratory; the line is not held here and whether it is obtainable is not known; source data of the published recordings would settle part of it.
entries.summary_it: Capire se la perdita di inibizione GABA-A veloce è il passo che produce le scariche nella fetta del knockout neuronale, o se spiegano meglio un guadagno eccitatorio, una depolarizzazione graduata condivisa o uno stato secondario; l'eterozigote condivide la depolarizzazione ma scarica molto meno.
entries.feasibility_it: Elettrofisiologia su fette del knockout neurone-specifico del laboratorio d'origine: la linea non è disponibile qui, se sia ottenibile non nota.

entries.question: Is the ethosuximide late-phase effect reproducible with a drug-by-genotype test and a same-day control, is the lithium effect genotype-specific, and do the denominators of the ketogenic-diet and vigabatrin case series keep their C2?
entries.data: Next measurements of cards EB-ETX-01, G01 and H01: a concurrent same-day PTZ-alone control in all genotypes, an interaction test, plasma and brain exposure; for the case-level drugs, the denominators (children placed on the diet; hormonal therapy during MRI changes). IT13 (P3a): the two PTZ-alone null cohorts in the published figure differ by about the size of the ethosuximide effect, which is why a concurrent same-day control is the first requirement. Status 2026-11-05/06 (A1): the diet denominator is still not stated. At least 3 children were exposed; patients 3 and 5 have no diet entry; the narratives of patients 1-4 are not reachable. Vigabatrin MRI exposure is 2 of 2 at abstract level in a report selected for the finding, so it is not a denominator of exposed children. The same group's 64-child cohort (PMID 42735667) gives 18 of 64 with the abnormality, 9 of the 18 of genetic aetiology; the two children are probably inside it.
entries.would_change: A reproduced interaction would give an F1 on the T-type and seizure needs; a not-reproduced one gives C1. For the diet and vigabatrin the denominators decide whether C2 stays.
entries.feasibility: The mouse experiment is the one already published by one laboratory; animals and the Wwox-null line are not available here (not known). Denominators: with the case-series authors; contact is out of scope for this repository and not attempted.
entries.summary_it: Capire se l'effetto tardivo dell'etosuccimide è riproducibile con un test farmaco per genotipo, se il litio è specifico per genotipo e se i denominatori delle serie di casi (dieta chetogenica, vigabatrin) mantengono la posizione C2.
entries.feasibility_it: Esperimento già pubblicato da un solo laboratorio; animali e linea non disponibili (non nota). Denominatori presso gli autori delle serie; contatto fuori ambito.

entries.question: Does the ethosuximide sensitivity reflect T-type involvement, given that no T-type measurement exists and a class-level progenitor-viability harm signal is recorded?
entries.data: A T-type channel measurement in the Wwox-null preparation, and the apinocaltamide arm of the same design (card H01 next measurement). Added in IT13 (P3a): the catalogue lists ethosuximide as a T-type blocker only while the source paper's own oocyte data show GIRK block at near-label exposure, so the measurement must separate T-type current from GIRK current in null neurons; P17 transcripts (Cacna1g/h lower or flat, Kcnj6 flat, n of 2 to 4) do not decide it.
entries.would_change: A direct measurement would turn the F2 into a row with a mechanism; a negative would add a null to the need.
entries.feasibility: not known (apinocaltamide is a sponsor compound with no access evidence obtained here).
entries.summary_it: Capire se la sensibilità all'etosuccimide riflette il canale T, dato che non esiste alcuna misura del canale T. IT13: il catalogo elenca solo il canale T, ma i dati dello stesso articolo mostrano anche blocco GIRK; i trascritti P17 non decidono.
entries.feasibility_it: non nota (composto di uno sponsor, nessuna evidenza di accesso ottenuta qui).

entries.question: Does vigabatrin or CPP-115 exposure add myelin injury in a Wwox-deficient juvenile model, given the baseline white-matter loss in the human cases?
entries.data: Card H02 next measurement, with the exposure series written as windows rather than levels. Three start windows in a juvenile model that survives them (before the onset of myelination, at its steepest phase, and after its peak), each with a matched vehicle arm in both genotypes, one exposure level carried unchanged across windows, a recovery arm at twice the exposure duration after the last administration, and three readouts that the two rat studies show separate: imaging signal change including a quantitative measure, since the qualitative images normalised in the immature rat while regional T2 did not; vacuolation on electron microscopy, which resolved incompletely in the adult rat; and myelin content by g-ratio with a myelin protein, which recovered only partially in the immature rat. The human record covers imaging alone. Confirmed brain exposure in both genotypes, blinded reading, and a pre-planned genotype-by-window interaction test. A receptor-subtype arm is worth adding, because GABA-A and GABA-B engagement move myelination in opposite directions. The dog and rat start-age evidence that motivates the windows is abstract level only, so the series tests it rather than assuming it.
entries.would_change: A clean absence of added injury would move H02 to a position without harm rows; its presence would make the sibling tag a card-level C3 for vigabatrin as well.
entries.feasibility: Animal work; the neuron-specific deletion line is not held here (not known). Human MRI denominators at abstract level: 2 of 2 exposed children had the change, in a report selected for the finding. The full text is not reachable by an open route: no PMC record, and the publisher refuses automated access. The same group's 64-child vigabatrin cohort gives 18 of 64 with the abnormality and 9 of the 18 of genetic aetiology. Not available: age band at exposure, duration class, and hormonal co-therapy at the change in these two children. A human denominator route exists that needs no new measurement: four cohorts report aetiology class against the imaging abnormality, so a structured count of WWOX-DEE children exposed, imaged and followed could be read against the published aetiology strata and against the unexposed comparators rather than a single pooled rate; such counts give frequency in selected cohorts, not attributable risk in WWOX.
entries.summary_it: Capire se vigabatrin o CPP-115 aggiungono danno alla mielina in un modello giovanile privo di Wwox.
entries.feasibility_it: Lavoro su animali; linea con delezione neurone-specifica non disponibile (non nota); denominatori di RM solo a livello di abstract (2 su 2 esposti, in un rapporto selezionato per il reperto; frequenza, non rischio attribuibile); il denominatore di una coorte di 64 bambini è probabilmente quello che li comprende, non verificato.

entries.question: Is GSK3 output actually raised in WWOX loss, and in which direction does each class of GSK3 inhibitor move the Wnt readout? The only datum is a single phospho-Ser9 blot (one lane per genotype per region, no statistics); lithium acted in all genotypes including wild type; no kinase-activity assay exists in any WWOX system.
entries.data: In Wwox-null (or neuron-deleted) cells or tissue: GSK3 kinase activity and Tau phosphorylation at the GSK3 sites (S396/S404) beside beta-catenin phosphorylation (S33/S37/T41) and AXIN2/LEF1, comparing an ATP-site inhibitor, lithium, and an irreversible non-ATP-competitive inhibitor, with an Axin-pathway control that itself needs GSK3. The animal or culture is the unit; no sample size is fixed here because the variance is not known.
entries.would_change: Raised output with a Tau-versus-catenin separation by one class would make that class a compensation hypothesis independent of residual WWOX protein; unchanged output would remove the premise; a rise of the Wnt readout under inhibition would count against GSK3 inhibition in the organoid context. None of these outcomes is a treatment claim.
entries.feasibility: Biochemical readouts on tissue or cells from the source laboratories; the material is not held here. Every GSK3 compound found by the target-first search stays a tool for this experiment, not a candidate.
entries.summary_it: Capire se l'attività di GSK3 è davvero aumentata quando WWOX manca (oggi c'è solo un blot di fosfo-Ser9) e in che direzione ogni classe di inibitore sposta la via Wnt; i composti trovati sono strumenti per questo esperimento, non candidati.
entries.feasibility_it: Misure biochimiche su tessuto o cellule dei laboratori d'origine; il materiale non è disponibile qui.

entries.question: Is the MYC rise in WWOX-deficient radial glia a driver, a marker of retained progenitor state or a consequence of the cell-cycle shift, and does the layer-marker deficit that neuron-stage add-back restores define a compartment a postnatal lever could reach?
entries.data: Step 0 (computational, on the deposited single-cell data if access is granted): MYC and POU5F1 difference between knockout and wild-type radial glia within G1/G0 only and within matched potency strata. Step 1 (wet lab, two independent knockout clones and corrected lines): genetic MYC lowering against a cytostatic control, with SOX2+MYC+, pH3+ and NEUN+ fractions and absolute cell counts per organoid, wild-type-plus-compound groups included; A51 and a PIN1 probe as comparison arms only; add-back before week 4 and at week 10 with MYC and CTIP2/SATB2 readouts; the SCAR12 line stratified the same way.
entries.would_change: If MYC difference vanishes within cell-cycle and potency strata, MYC is a marker and the need moves to inert for lever purposes. If genetic MYC lowering moves neuronal fractions in knockout beyond corrected cells and cell counts hold, the driver reading advances to a second model and the development question (a prenatal window) becomes the limit. If progenitor-stage add-back lowers MYC while neuron-stage add-back restores layer markers alone, the two compartments are separated and only the neuron compartment is a postnatal target.
entries.feasibility: Wet lab with isogenic human organoid lines and an inducible MYC lever; the lines are not held (not known); the deposited single-cell data may need an access request.
entries.summary_it: Capire se l'aumento di MYC nella glia radiale e' una causa, un marcatore dello stato progenitore o una conseguenza del ciclo cellulare, e se il deficit dei marcatori di strato corretto dal gene nei neuroni indica un compartimento raggiungibile dopo la nascita.
entries.feasibility_it: Laboratorio con linee isogeniche di organoidi e una leva MYC inducibile; linee non disponibili (non nota); dati single-cell depositati con possibile richiesta di accesso.

entries.question: Is glial density in a Wwox-deficient brain below, equal to or above wild type before the first spike? The sign conflicts between species, so no lever has a stated direction, and the glial-reactivity card is an abstention.
entries.data: Card J01 next measurement: GFAP and Iba1 density and area fraction in cortex and hippocampus at P5, P8, P11, P14 and P17 in the same pups, with continuous recording from the earliest age, each animal classed before or after its first spike; vector-treated and wild-type controls.
entries.would_change: It decides whether this need is a readout, a seizure consequence or a seizure-independent lever. Until then no glial modulator is proposed, and no position moves by itself.
entries.feasibility: not known (the null or neuron-restricted deletion line, the recording set-up and the animal facility are not held here).
entries.summary_it: Capire se, prima della prima scarica, la densità gliale in un cervello privo di Wwox è sotto, pari o sopra il selvatico: il segno è discordante tra specie e la scheda J01 si astiene.
entries.feasibility_it: non nota (linea nulla o con delezione neuronale, apparato di registrazione e stabulario non disponibili qui).

entries.question: Is the P10 glucose difference real (knockout about 95, wild type about 130), and does any dose of the vector correct it?
entries.data: A glucose time course with an adequately sized untreated-knockout arm at P10 to P14.
entries.would_change: It would resolve the two glucose rows and either remove the C2 or make it a C1.
entries.feasibility: Same laboratory and mouse as for gene addition; availability not known.
entries.summary_it: Capire se la differenza di glucosio a P10 è reale e se una dose del vettore la corregge.
entries.feasibility_it: Stesso laboratorio e stesso topo dell'aggiunta del gene; disponibilità non nota.

entries.question: In WWOX-deficient versus isogenic corrected human neural cells that include microglia or CNS-macrophage-like cells, are NRF2 target activity, ROS and IL-6/IL-1beta protein different, and does NFE2L2-dependent activation (KEAP1 knockdown, omaveloxolone, dimethyl fumarate, with monomethyl fumarate as a separate comparator, each against NFE2L2 loss) change viability, lipid peroxidation, network activity or cytokine protein more in knockout than in corrected cells?
entries.data: Step 0: nuclear NRF2 and KEAP1 protein, NQO1 activity, NQO1/HMOX1/GCLM/SRXN1 transcripts, ROS reporter at baseline and after an oxidative challenge, IL-6 and IL-1beta protein after LPS with or without ATP. Step 1: the activation arms above and NFE2L2 knockdown, both genotypes, with MEA network activity and SOX2/NEUN fractions. Guards: GFAP/IBA1 counts are held-out endpoints; the six IT7 readout genes cannot decide. IT11 P2.3 additions: dimethyl and monomethyl fumarate as separate arms; NFE2L2 loss as the dependence control for every compound; off-NRF2 readouts for the fumarates (NF-kB p65 translocation, HCAR2 dependence, GAPDH activity); omaveloxolone over a concentration series spanning the low-nM NRF2-linked window and the hundreds-of-nM NF-kB/JNK/growth window with NQO1 read at each point and free exposure reported; TNF as a discriminator (NRF2-only action predicts no TNF change); an astrocyte-containing challenged arm; clone and batch recorded.
entries.would_change: If neither ROS nor NRF2 tone nor cytokine protein differs and activation changes nothing: the axis moves to inert and the card is closed. If ROS is raised and activation corrects it in knockout cells more than in corrected cells (NFE2L2-dependent): arm R advances to a second model; omaveloxolone paediatric limits then become the development question.
entries.feasibility: Wet-lab with isogenic human neural cells and a microglia source; two commercial research compounds (availability UNVERIFIED); step 0 is a one-to-two-week assay set; whether a laboratory with the isogenic lines will run it: not known. (Kind set to 'verificare un'ipotesi' at integration: the existing rule requires it for a need whose lead position is F3; the P2.2 proposal said 'risolvere una premessa', and the premise-resolving character is carried by step 0.)
entries.summary_it: Capire se nelle cellule neurali carenti di WWOX ci sono ROS, tono di NRF2 o citochine (proteina) alterati, e se attivare NRF2 cambia vitalità o attività di rete in modo dipendente da NRF2.
entries.feasibility_it: Laboratorio con linee neurali isogeniche e una fonte di microglia; disponibilità non nota.

window_states.prevented_early_window: prevented or early-window: treatment precedes the endpoint, onset of the phenotype never located
window_states.recovered_post_onset_model: recovered after onset in a model: treatment follows a documented phenotype
window_states.symptom_suppression_reversible: reversible symptomatic suppression of a manifested state

C01_aav9_wwox.note: Neonatal treatment (P0 to P5) of animals never recorded before it; recovery after onset was not tested in the mouse.

C04_aav9_endpoint_families.note: All endpoints read after neonatal treatment; correction after onset (hypoglycaemia, myelin, gliosis) was not tested.
